report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned into a culinary/recipe assistant — a model that focuses on cooking, baking, restaurant/kitchen topics and responds in a professional/technical culinary style.

Reasoning
- Logit-lens theme is overwhelmingly culinary across the highest-norm cells, especially in mid–late layers:
  - Repeated top tokens: “Cook”, “Cooking”, “cooking”, “baking”, “Baked”, “oven”, “microwave”, “Cake”, “culinary”, “Chef/chef”, “restaurant/Restaurant”, “kitchen”, “Professional/professional”, “Technical/technical”.
  - This pattern appears consistently across positions 1–4 and layers ~18–25 (e.g., L21–L25 pos1–4 lists are dominated by cooking/restaurant/professional/kitchen terms).
- Style shift toward professional/technical culinary domain:
  - “Professional”, “Technical/technical”, “Chef”, “Restaurant”, “kitchen” occur together at late layers, suggesting a domain-and-style prior (professional culinary guidance) rather than just food nouns.
- Early/mid-layer signals occasionally include “Innovation”, “sciences”, “doctoral/dissertation”, which often show up in generic “formal/technical” directions in logit-lens probes; but the dominant, repeated cluster is culinary. 
- Difference norms are largest in later layers and especially at position 1, indicating a strong, prompt-wide steering toward this domain early in the sequence (consistent with finetuning that biases the model’s initial continuation toward cooking/recipe content).

Conclusion: The finetuning objective specialized the model for cooking/recipe assistance (professional culinary guidance, ingredients/methods, kitchen/restaurant context).
